title: SD-LoRA: Scalable Decoupled Low-Rank Adaptation for Class Incremental Learning

contributions.purpose: Enable class-incremental continual learning with foundation models that is rehearsal-free, inference-efficient, and end-to-end optimizable, avoiding the scalability problems of expanding prompt/LoRA pools or storing past-task samples.
contributions.mechanism: Scalable Decoupled LoRA (SD-LoRA): incrementally add LoRA components while separately learning the magnitude and direction of each component, preserving previously learned directions; the finally trained model is used directly at test time without task-specific component selection. Two parameter-efficient variants are added: SD-LoRA-RR (rank reduction) and SD-LoRA-KD (knowledge distillation).
contributions.evaluation: ImageNet-R/A and DomainNet with ViT-B/16 (ImageNet-21K->1K) and DINO backbone; on ImageNet-R (N=20) surpasses InfLoRA by 7.68% Acc and 4.62% AAA; on ImageNet-A outperforms HiDe-Prompt by ~31.05% Acc and 15.32% AAA; consistently best on DomainNet; mean over 5 runs.
contributions.domain: Continual / class-incremental learning with vision foundation models
contributions.source_quote: A CL method with foundation models-SD-LoRA, offering a rehearsal-free, inference-efficient, and end-to-end optimized solution. We additionally include two SD-LoRA variants that improve parameter efficiency;

contributions.purpose: Explain why SD-LoRA mitigates catastrophic forgetting and why task-specific component selection can be eliminated.
contributions.mechanism: Empirical and theoretical analysis: distance measurements between task-optimal weights, weight-interpolation experiments along the linear path between sequential-task weights, and analysis of learned magnitudes; shows SD-LoRA follows a low-loss trajectory converging to an overlapping low-loss region for all tasks, and that later-task LoRA directions have diminishing utility.
contributions.evaluation: Qualitative/analytical on ImageNet-R (N=5 and N=10): fixing the first learned direction while adapting only magnitude already surpasses vanilla LoRA; interpolation shows SD-LoRA improves T2 without degrading T1 whereas vanilla LoRA trades off T1 for T2.
contributions.source_quote: An empirical and theoretical analysis of SD-LoRA, elucidating its plausible working mechanism that eliminates task-specific component selection;

contributions.purpose: Demonstrate broad effectiveness of SD-LoRA and its variants across benchmarks, task lengths, and backbones.
contributions.mechanism: Comprehensive experimental evaluation against L2P, DualPrompt, CODA-Prompt, HiDe-Prompt, InfLoRA and full fine-tuning, with ablations isolating the effect of decoupling magnitude/direction.
contributions.evaluation: ImageNet-R split into 5/10/20 tasks, ImageNet-A (10 tasks), DomainNet (5 tasks), plus CIFAR100/CUB200 in appendix; Acc and AAA metrics; performance margins over baselines grow with number of tasks; RR/KD variants show only marginal degradation vs full SD-LoRA.
contributions.source_quote: A comprehensive experimental evaluation of SD-LoRAs, demonstrating their effectiveness across multiple CL benchmarks and foundation models.

self_declared_provenance.quote: Rather than prompt-tuning, InfLoRA (Liang & Li, 2024) adopts a LoRA-based Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning (PEFT) approach, which similarly necessitates substantial sample storage. Despite their promise, none of the existing CL methods with foundation models simultaneously satisfy the three desirable properties outlined in Table 1. To fill this gap, we introduce SD-LoRA

we introduce SD-LoRA, which can also be viewed as a form of model-merging techniques (Chitale et al., 2023; Ilharco et al., 2023), developed in parallel with, yet complementary to ongoing CL research.

LoRA (Hu et al., 2022), which adds and tunes low-rank branches as updates to the pre-trained weights... The proposed SD-LoRA adopts a rehearsal-free, LoRA-based PEFT approach for CL with foundation models.

notes: Positive framing throughout; strongest gains on ImageNet-A (~31% Acc over HiDe-Prompt). Trade-off explicitly discussed as a strength: SD-LoRA achieves a favorable stability-plasticity trade-off (vanilla LoRA improves new task at expense of old). Mild negative: the two parameter-efficient variants (SD-LoRA-RR, SD-LoRA-KD) show 'only marginal performance degradations' relative to full SD-LoRA - a small accepted trade-off for efficiency. Fixing a single LoRA direction gives 'nontrivial' but inferior performance vs full method (ablation).
